chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have dedicated a third of my supplications to you.' He said to him, 'Good.' The man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have dedicated half of my supplications to you.' He said to him, 'That is better.' The man said, 'I have dedicated all of my supplications to you.' He said, 'Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will suffice you from whatever concerns you regarding the affairs of your world and your Hereafter.'

A man said to him, 'May Allah keep you well, how does he dedicate his supplication to him?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for anything except that he begins with the supplication (Salat) upon Muhammad and his Family (peace be upon them).'
ai.seo_question: How does dedicating prayers to the Prophet ensure acceptance of supplications?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that 'dedicating' one's prayers to the Prophet is not a transfer of divine favor, but a method of prioritization: the supplicant begins every petition with Salawat, thereby honoring the intercessor first. This practice ensures that God suffices the believer from worldly and otherworldly anxieties, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt as the spiritual conduit for divine grace. The hadith underscores the theological principle that seeking closeness to God through the Prophet's household is a means of securing comprehensive divine care.
